source: SDAIA AI Bias Reference Guide, first edition (May 2026). Names and pages as in the guide; the one-line summaries are the course's own words. Read the guide's entry before tagging.

types.name: Age Bias
types.summary: Outcomes are less accurate or fair for an age group: the guide stresses older people under-represented in the data, and designs that ignore age-related differences

types.name: Aggregation Bias
types.summary: Groups that differ are pooled into one model, which then fits the largest groups best

types.name: Automation Bias
types.summary: People defer to a system's output even where their own judgement or other evidence should prevail

types.name: Concept Drift
types.summary: The relation between inputs and the target changes over time, so learnt patterns stop holding

types.name: Coverage Bias
types.summary: The data do not represent the full population the system is used on

types.name: Evaluation Bias
types.summary: The data or metrics used to judge a system do not reflect the cases it will meet, so its performance is overstated

types.name: Gender Bias
types.summary: A system's outcomes unfairly favour one gender, often through unrepresentative data or embedded stereotypes

types.name: Historical Bias
types.summary: The data carry past conditions or decisions that no longer hold

types.name: Measurement Bias
types.summary: Values are systematically recorded too high or too low

types.name: Model Drift
types.summary: Performance deteriorates over time as the data or the environment changes

types.name: Overconfidence Bias
types.summary: A system or its developers overstate how accurate it is

types.name: Sample Size Bias
types.summary: A sample too small (or badly sized) for reliable learning or validation

types.name: Socioeconomic Bias
types.summary: Outcomes differ by economic status because some groups are under-represented or their traits disfavoured
